page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-8 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. It features 8 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 30.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 3.75 GB of memory per core. It contains no bundled local storage or GPUs, and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8) for hardware-accelerated matrix operations. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2256.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 15.25 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression is also strong at 35.04 GB/sec. Multi-core performance scales to average levels, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8502.0 and a multi-core stress-ng CPU performance score of 8882.75.

Memory performance is characterized by a cached small-block read bandwidth of 690.5 GB/sec, which drops to 61.57 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. The server handles light machine learning workloads efficiently, achieving a top-tier text generation speed of 352.64 tokens/sec on a small 135M parameter LLM. However, resource limitations are evident on larger models, where text generation speed drops to a weak 7.21 tokens/sec for a medium 7B parameter model. Given the dedicated compute resources and advanced instruction sets, this instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, text processing, software compilation, and lightweight vector-accelerated tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-8 is an x86_64 general-purpose server featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz, paired with 30.0 GB of RAM. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. In benchmarks, the server exhibits top-tier single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2256.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression of 15.25 GB/sec. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth align with mid-range expectations, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 8502.0. While highly capable at processing smaller language models, performance degrades significantly on larger models. This configuration is suited for text processing, software compilation, and general-purpose workloads requiring dedicated compute cores without local storage requirements.
